blocks.task_summary: Use the quadratic model y = -0.6T^2 + 23T + 110 to estimate the number of children y when the highest temperature T = 25 deg C.

evidence.basis: recognising to find y(25) (M1); y(25) = -0.6 x 25^2 + 23 x 25 + 110 = 310 (children) A1

blocks.task_summary: Find a regression equation to predict ice creams sold x from the total number of children y, using the given five-pair data set.
method_path: recognise that x-on-y regression is required to predict x from y
use GDC to compute linear regression of x on y, obtaining a=0.0935114, b=7.43053

evidence.basis: recognizing x on y is required (M1); 0.0935114 and 7.43053 (A1); x = 0.0935y + 7.43 A1

blocks.task_summary: Use the regression equation from part (b) with y=310 from part (a) to predict the number of ice creams sold x when T=25 deg C.
method_path: substitute y=310 into regression equation x=0.0935y+7.43
accepted_alternatives: Use y-on-x regression y=9.39x-41.5 from part (b), substitute y=310, solve to get x=37

evidence.basis: attempt to substitute their answer to part (a) into their regression equation (M1); x = 0.0935114 x 310 + 7.43053 = 36.4190 = 36 (accept 37 or 36.4) A1; Note: Award (M1)A1FT for x=37 found from using y=9.39x-41.5; Award (M1)A0FT for a correct FT answer that lies outside [15,46]
